company: Brightdesk (a made-up shared-inbox app sold per seat). Replace everything in this file with your own.

views.name: catalog_accounts
views.description: One row per customer account with its owner email (when the account has a Stripe customer) and is_internal = our own QA, test and staff accounts. Catalog metrics exclude is_internal accounts through this view; it is the one place that holds the test-account list.

metrics.name: new_paying_customers
metrics.description: Accounts that paid their first-ever invoice in the week, Monday to Monday, UTC. A $0 invoice paid by coupon counts. Test and staff accounts are excluded.
metrics.reasoning: Same rule as the weekly KPI report's new-customers column: first-ever paid invoice, half-open Monday week in UTC. Checked account by account against the report's own list for three weeks before proposing.

metrics.name: new_seats
metrics.description: Seats bought on each account's first subscription, counted in the week the subscription was created, Monday to Monday, UTC. Later upgrades and subscriptions that started as a free trial are not included. Test and staff accounts are excluded.
metrics.reasoning: The synced Stripe subscription row holds today's quantity, after upgrades, so seats come from the subscription's first invoice (billing_reason = subscription_create). Matches the weekly report for the weeks checked.

metrics.name: website_visitors
metrics.description: Unique visitors of the marketing site in the week, Monday to Monday, UTC.
metrics.reasoning: Written in SQL so the week starts on Monday; a Trends query follows the project's week, which starts on Sunday by default. Counted by pageview time, so it can differ from the Web analytics page by a few people.

metrics.name: hubspot_new_connections
metrics.description: Accounts that connected HubSpot for the first time ever in the week, Monday to Monday, UTC. Reconnects do not count. Test and staff accounts are excluded.
metrics.reasoning: First-ever hubspot_connected per account. A connection is recreated on every reconnect, so counting events in the week would count reconnects.

metrics.name: zapier_new_connections
metrics.description: Accounts that subscribed their first-ever Zapier trigger in the week, Monday to Monday, UTC. Later subscriptions by the same account do not count. Test and staff accounts are excluded.
metrics.reasoning: The team says 'Zapier connections' for two different numbers. This one is new connections; zapier_trigger_subscribers is activity. Two honest names instead of one contested metric.

metrics.name: zapier_trigger_subscribers
metrics.description: People who subscribed a Zapier trigger in the week, Monday to Monday, UTC, repeat subscriptions included. Test and staff accounts are excluded.
metrics.reasoning: The activity meaning of 'Zapier connections', kept under its own name so that a question about new connections does not land here.

metrics.name: signups
metrics.description: New accounts created in the week, Monday to Monday, UTC. Test and staff accounts are excluded.
metrics.reasoning: The app database is not synced into PostHog, so this entry tells the agent where the canonical number is. The signed_up event runs a few percent below it.

metrics.name: mailbox_connections
metrics.description: Accounts that connected a mailbox for the first time ever in the week, Monday to Monday, UTC. Reconnects do not count. Test and staff accounts are excluded.
metrics.reasoning: Computed from the app database. The mailbox_connected event misses several ways of connecting and runs well below the report, so the steps forbid it.

certifications.notes: Use for every customer or account count: is_internal = 1 marks QA, test and staff accounts. The one place that holds the test-account list; add a new test account here, not in a metric.

Source for paid-customer counts. The paid date is status_transitions.paid_at (created_at only when paid_at is empty). Seats at purchase: lines of the invoice with billing_reason = subscription_create.
metadata.account_id is the account. A customer without account_id is not a product account (partner or manual invoice). One customer is one account.
quantity is today's seat count, after any upgrade, and status is today's status. For seats at purchase read the subscription's first invoice in stripe.invoice.

relationships.reasoning: Paid-customer metrics go from an invoice to its customer to find the account.
Seat metrics go from a subscription to its customer to find the account.
Lets any query drop internal accounts with customer.account.is_internal instead of copying the test-account list.
